planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall into consistently moist, humus-rich soil in part to full shade; keep margin color brightest by avoiding hot afternoon sun.

directions: Georgia Sweetheart is the full-sized hosta from which the dwarf sport 'Georgia Satellite' arose, forming a fuller mound of green-centered leaves trimmed in a bold yellow-orange edge. Its broader, more open foliage and taller stature set it apart from the tightly twisted, miniature habit of its sport. Like most hostas it sends up pale lavender, bell-shaped flowers on scapes above the foliage in summer. Grow in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in part to full shade to keep the margin color vivid and prevent leaf scorch.
